text: Quickstart lets you get an API key and store/search your first memory within minutes
quote: In about five minutes you will get an API key, store your first memory, and search it back.

text: MCP server exposes memory tools so an agent can autonomously save, look up, or update its own memories
quote: The Mem0 MCP server hands your agent a set of memory tools, so it can decide for itself when to save something, look something up, or update what it already knows.

text: A coding agent can create its own account and API key from the terminal with a few commands, no email or dashboard needed
quote: Four terminal commands create an account and API key. No email, no dashboard.

text: Open-source version runs the same memory engine on your own infrastructure, giving full ownership of stack and data
quote: Mem0 Open Source is the same memory engine as the Platform, running on your own infrastructure. You own the stack, the data, and every component

text: Self-hosted Docker bundle ships REST API, dashboard, per-user API keys, and a request audit log
quote: A Docker stack with a dashboard, per-user API keys, and a request audit log.

text: Natural-language search lets agents query stored memories and get back the most relevant ones
quote: Mem0's search operation lets agents ask natural-language questions and get back the memories that matter most.

text: Platform automatically builds a native graph linking people, places and concepts from memories, with no external graph database to run
quote: Mem0 Platform builds a native graph linking people, places, and concepts across your memories, with no external graph database to provision.

text: Memories can be scoped separately per user, agent, and application so retrieval stays isolated per tenant
quote: Mem0's Platform API lets you separate memories for different users, agents, and apps.

text: Reranking step reorders search results using deep semantic understanding to surface the most relevant memories first
quote: Reorders results using deep semantic understanding to put the most relevant memories first.

text: Setting an expiration_date on a memory stops it from being surfaced in search after that date, without deleting it
quote: Set an expiration date on a Mem0 memory and it stops surfacing in search once that date passes. Nothing is deleted.

text: Memory Export feature creates structured exports of memories using customizable Pydantic schemas
quote: The Memory Export feature allows you to create structured exports of memories using customizable Pydantic schemas.

text: Webhooks send real-time HTTP notifications when memories are created, updated, deleted, or categorized
quote: You can configure webhooks to send HTTP POST requests to your specified URLs whenever memories are created, updated, deleted, or categorized.

text: Official CLI supports adding, searching, listing, updating, and deleting memories directly from the terminal
quote: The mem0 CLI lets you add, search, list, update, and delete memories directly from the terminal.

text: Documented setup guides cover 22 integrations including LangChain, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, and the Vercel AI SDK
quote: Setup guides for 22 tools, including LangChain, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, and the Vercel AI SDK.

text: Plugins let coding tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex remember project context via shared memory
quote: Plugins that let Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and other harnesses remember your project.

text: Any AI client can be connected to Mem0 via the Model Context Protocol in minutes
quote: Connect any AI client to Mem0 using Model Context Protocol in minutes

text: Mem0 automatically extracts individual facts from a conversation and stores each one separately
quote: Mem0 pulls the individual facts out of the conversation and stores each one separately

text: SDK provides a simple add call (e.g. client.add(messages, user_id=...)) for storing conversation memories per user
Users can ask entity-centric questions (e.g. 'what do we know about Alice') and get facts pulled from many past conversations
quote: You ask entity-centric questions like "what do we know about Alice?" and expect facts pulled from many different conversations
